cases.sentence: Отворилась тугая наружная стеклянная ___ на улицу и туго захлопнулась.
cases.translation: The heavy outer glass door onto the street opened and slammed shut again.
cases.explain: «Дверь» is the grammatical subject of the intransitive verb «отворилась» (opened), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Я стоялась у ___ возле стула, на котором она сидела, и бессмысленно смотрел перед собой.
cases.translation: I stood by the table, near the chair where she had been sitting, and stared blankly ahead.
cases.explain: The preposition «у» (by/near) always governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: По ___ поминутно подходил к ширмам и в щелочку поглядывал на Лизу.
cases.translation: Every minute I walked around the room, went up to the screen, and peeked through the crack at Liza.
cases.explain: «По» meaning movement around/along a surface governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Отворилась тугая наружная стеклянная дверь на ___ и туго захлопнулась.
cases.translation: The heavy outer glass door onto the street opened and slammed shut again.
cases.explain: «На» with a noun expressing the direction a door opens onto takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Через четверть часа я бегал взад и вперед с бешеным ___.
cases.translation: A quarter of an hour later I was pacing back and forth with furious impatience.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» meaning «with» (manner) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Это была там бумажка, другой и быть не могло, другой и в ___ не было.
cases.translation: It was that same banknote lying there — there could not have been another one, and there was no other one in the house.
cases.explain: «В» expressing static location (not motion) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Она сидела на полу, склонив на кровать голову и, должно быть, плакала.
reading.question: What was Liza doing while sitting on the floor?
options: Crying with her head bowed to the bed
reading.correct: Crying with her head bowed to the bed
reading.explain: The text says she sat on the floor with her head bowed to the bed, apparently crying.

reading.ru: Она догадалась, что порыв моей страсти был именно мщением, новым ей унижением, и что к давешней моей почти беспредметной ненависти прибавилась теперь уже личная, зависывая к ней, ненависть.
reading.question: What did Liza realize about the narrator's passion?
options: It was revenge and a fresh humiliation of her
reading.correct: It was revenge and a fresh humiliation of her
reading.explain: She guessed that the outburst of his passion was actually revenge, a new humiliation for her.

reading.ru: Во-первых, я и полюбить уже не мог, потому что, повторю, любить у меня значило тиранствовать и нравственно превосходствовать.
reading.question: What did "loving" mean to the narrator?
options: Tyrannizing and morally dominating the other person
reading.correct: Tyrannizing and morally dominating the other person
reading.explain: He states plainly that for him loving meant to tyrannize and morally dominate.

reading.ru: Ай, не догадался сам, что она пришла вовсе не для того, чтобы жалкие слова слушать, а чтобы любить меня, потому что для женщины любви-то и заключается всё воскресенье, всё спасение от какой бы то ни было гибели и всё возрождение, да иначе и проявиться не может, как в этом.
reading.question: Why had Liza really come, according to the narrator's belated realization?
reading.correct: To love him
reading.explain: He realizes she came not to hear pitiful words but to love him.

reading.ru: Я хотел, чтобы она исчезла.
reading.question: What did the narrator say he wanted?
reading.correct: For Liza to disappear
reading.explain: He directly states, "I wanted her to disappear."

reading.ru: Она вдруг встрепенулась, схватилась с места и бросилась искать свой платок, свою шляпку, шубу, точно спасаясь от меня.
reading.question: How did Liza react, as if escaping from him?
options: She jumped up and searched for her things
reading.correct: She jumped up and searched for her things
reading.explain: She suddenly started up and rushed to look for her kerchief, hat, and coat, as if escaping from him.

reading.ru: «Прощайте», — проговорила она, направляясь к двери.
reading.question: What did Liza say as she headed for the door?
reading.correct: "Прощайте" (Farewell)
reading.explain: The text quotes her saying "Прощайте" (Farewell) as she moved toward the door.

reading.ru: Я вдруг подбежал к ней, схватил ее руку, разжал ее и вложил, и потом опять зажал.
reading.question: What did the narrator do to Liza's hand?
options: He opened it, put something in it, and closed it again
reading.correct: He opened it, put something in it, and closed it again
reading.explain: He ran up, grabbed her hand, opened it, put something inside, and closed it again.

reading.ru: Не помню себя, потерявшись в дуру, но я не хочу гадить, и потому говорю прямо, что я разжал ей руку и положил в нее со злости.
reading.question: According to the narrator's own admission, in what spirit did he put money in her hand?
reading.correct: Out of malice
reading.explain: He admits he opened her hand and put the money in it out of spite/malice ("со злости").

reading.ru: Лиза, Лиза, крикнула на лестницу, но не смела в полголоса.
reading.question: What did the narrator do on the stairwell?
options: He ran past her without a word
reading.correct: He called out Liza's name
reading.explain: He shouted "Liza, Liza" down the stairwell, though not daring to do it loudly.

reading.ru: Отворилась тугая наружная стеклянная дверь на улицу и туго захлопнулась.
reading.question: What sound confirmed that Liza had left the building?
options: The heavy glass street door opening and slamming shut
reading.correct: The heavy glass street door opening and slamming shut
reading.explain: He heard the heavy outer glass door onto the street open and then slam shut.

reading.ru: Прямо перед собой на столе я увидал, одним словом, я видел смятую синюю пятирублевую бумажку, ту самую, которую минуту назад зажал в ее руке.
reading.question: What did the narrator suddenly see on the table?
reading.correct: A crumpled blue five-ruble note
reading.explain: He suddenly saw a crumpled blue five-ruble note on the table, the very one he had pressed into her hand.

reading.ru: Она 200 шагов еще не успела уйти, когда я выбежал на улицу.
reading.question: How far had Liza gotten before the narrator ran out into the street?
options: She was still inside the building
reading.correct: Less than 200 steps
reading.explain: The text says she had not yet managed to go 200 steps when he ran out into the street.

reading.ru: Было тихо, валил снег и падал почти перпендикулярно, настилая подушку на тротуар и на пустынную улицу.
reading.question: What was the weather like when the narrator ran outside?
options: Snow falling almost straight down, blanketing the empty street
reading.correct: Snow falling almost straight down, blanketing the empty street
reading.explain: It was quiet, snow was falling almost perpendicularly, laying a blanket on the sidewalk and the empty street.

reading.ru: Упасть перед ней, зарыдать от раскаяния, целовать ее ноги, молить о прощении.
reading.question: What did the narrator imagine doing before Liza?
options: Falling before her, weeping in repentance, kissing her feet, begging forgiveness
reading.correct: Falling before her, weeping in repentance, kissing her feet, begging forgiveness
reading.explain: He imagines falling before her, sobbing with repentance, kissing her feet, and begging forgiveness.

reading.ru: Разве я не возненавижу ее, может быть, завтра же именно за то, что сегодня целовал ее ноги?
reading.question: What does the narrator fear he might feel toward Liza as soon as tomorrow?
options: Hatred, precisely because he kissed her feet today
reading.correct: Hatred, precisely because he kissed her feet today
reading.explain: He wonders whether he will not come to hate her tomorrow precisely because he kissed her feet today.

reading.ru: И не лучше ли будет, фантазировал я уже дома, после заглушения фантазиями живую сердечную боль, не лучше ли будет, если она навеки унесет теперь с собой оскорбление?
reading.question: What does the narrator wonder might be "better" for Liza to carry away with her forever?
reading.correct: A sense of insult/offense
reading.explain: He wonders whether it would be better if she carried away the insult forever.

reading.ru: Никогда больше я не встречал Лизу, я ничего не слыхал о ней.
reading.question: What happened to Liza after that night, according to the narrator?
options: He never saw or heard of her again
She wrote him letters for years
reading.correct: He never saw or heard of her again
reading.explain: He states he never met Liza again and never heard anything about her.

reading.ru: Мне кажется, я сделал ошибку, начав их писать.
reading.question: What does the narrator say he regrets?
reading.correct: Beginning to write these notes
reading.explain: He says he thinks he made a mistake in starting to write these notes.

reading.ru: В романе надо героя, а тут нарочно собраны все черты для антигероя.
reading.question: What does the narrator say a novel needs, which his own story deliberately lacks?
options: A hero — his notes instead gather traits of an anti-hero
reading.correct: A hero — his notes instead gather traits of an anti-hero
reading.explain: He says a novel needs a hero, while here all the traits of an anti-hero were deliberately gathered instead.

reading.ru: Мы даже и человеками-то быть тяготимся, человеками с настоящим собственным телом и кровью, стыдимся этого, за позор считаем и норовим быть какими-то небывалыми общечеловеками.
reading.question: What does the narrator say people are even burdened by being?
options: Being human beings with real flesh and blood
reading.correct: Being human beings with real flesh and blood
reading.explain: He says people are even weary of being human beings with real bodies and blood, and are ashamed of it.
